sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/autocomplete-for-woo-orders/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  3. Go to WooCommerce → Smart Autocomplete
  4. Enable your automation rules
  5. Orders will now complete automatically after payment

Use Cases

  • Digital Product Stores (eBooks, PDFs, Music, Software): Instantly complete orders after payment so customers get immediate access to downloads without manual intervention.

  • Online Courses & LMS Platforms: Automatically mark orders as completed to trigger course enrollment, lesson access, or student dashboards right after checkout.

  • Membership & Subscription Websites: Enable seamless access to premium content by auto-completing paid orders for members and subscribers.

  • High-Volume WooCommerce Stores: Save hours of admin time by auto-completing thousands of paid orders daily—ideal for stores processing 20,000+ orders.

  • Virtual Service Providers: Auto-complete orders for consultations, digital services, or online bookings where shipping is not required.

  • Event Tickets & Webinar Sales: Instantly confirm attendance and send access details after successful payment without manual order handling.

  • Print-on-Demand & Dropshipping Stores: Auto-complete prepaid orders to streamline fulfillment workflows and reduce order processing delays.

  • Multi-Gateway Payment Stores: Apply smart rules based on payment methods (PayPal, Stripe, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna, etc.) for safer automation.

  • Hybrid Stores (Physical + Digital Products): Automatically complete digital-only orders while keeping physical product orders under manual review.

Supported product types

  • – Types: Simple, Simple Virtual, Simple Virtual & Downloadable

  • – Optional (Pro): Variable, Variable Virtual, Variable Virtual & Downloadable

Lightweight

  • Runs only when WooCommerce reports a completed payment

  • Works with most popular WordPress themes, HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) and both the classic and the block checkout

sections.faq:
Does this plugin automatically complete WooCommerce orders?

Yes. Orders are automatically marked as Completed after successful payment, based on your configured rules.

Which product types are supported?

Simple, Virtual, Downloadable, and Virtual + Downloadable products. Variable products are available in the Pro version.

Does it work with physical products?

Only if you tick “Simple product orders (includes physical products)”. It is off by default on new installs, so physical orders stay in Processing until you ship them. Tick it only if you want physical orders completed right after payment.

Does it work with Cash on Delivery or Bank Transfer?

No. Cash on delivery, bank transfer and cheque orders are not paid when they are placed, so WooCommerce never reports a completed payment for them and the plugin leaves them untouched.

Does the “Enable” switch really turn everything off?

Yes. With the switch off the plugin never changes an order status.

Can I run the Free and the Pro version together?

No need to. When the Pro version is active and licensed it replaces this plugin and the Free version steps aside. If Pro is installed without a licence, the Free version keeps working and its settings page is listed as “Smart Autocomplete (Free)”.

Which payment gateways are supported?

All gateways that mark orders as paid, including PayPal, Stripe, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Amazon Pay, Klarna, Afterpay, Venmo, and more.

Will WooCommerce emails still be sent?

Yes. All default WooCommerce emails continue to work normally.

sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Fix: the “Enable Smart Autocomplete” switch now really turns the plugin off. Before, orders could still be completed with the switch off.
  • Fix: new installs no longer complete physical product orders. They start with virtual and virtual + downloadable orders only. Existing settings are not changed.
  • Fix: unpaid orders (cash on delivery, bank transfer, cheque, pending payments) are never completed. The extra checkout hook and the “needs processing” override that could bypass the payment-method, role and enable rules were removed.
  • Fix: deactivating the plugin no longer deletes its settings, and “Delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted” now works on uninstall (it read the wrong option before). Uninstall also removes the saved settings tab, the review-notice flag and the order markers, on every site of a multisite network.
  • Fix: the “completed by this plugin” marker is no longer written while WooCommerce is only asking for a status. It is now saved as order meta after the payment completes, so it works with HPOS and leaves no orphaned rows when an order is deleted. Orders marked by older versions still show the thank-you message.
  • Fix: the thank-you message only appears on orders that really were completed by the plugin.
  • Fix: guest checkouts now count as the “Customer” role when role rules are used.
  • Fix: the plugin works when WooCommerce is network-activated and when the Pro version is installed. Free steps aside for a licensed Pro, and uses its own settings page and menu name while Pro is present, so the two pages no longer render on top of each other.
  • Fix: the plugin version constant now matches the plugin version, so updated CSS and JS are not served from old caches.
  • Fix: the class guard had a typo, which could cause a “cannot redeclare class” error when the file loaded twice.
  • Fix: the settings page remembers the active tab after saving (two different names were used before).
  • Fix: dismissing the review notice now requires the manage_woocommerce capability.
  • Fix: PHP notices and a possible fatal error on the orders list (missing setting and missing order). The Payment Method column now follows its setting on both order screens, and the sorting that never worked was removed.
  • Improvement: the thank-you box uses a CSS file instead of long inline styles, and the settings labels are clearer (“Simple product orders (includes physical products)”, “Delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted”).
  • Cleanup: removed unused code (public asset loader, unused AJAX nonce, empty catch blocks) and unsupported performance claims from this readme.
